welcome.title: Your atelier, without the paper
welcome.body: TailorCraft keeps your clients, measurements, orders, fittings and payments in one place on your phone. This short guide shows how everything fits together.
welcome.p1: Set up your garments: the pieces you make, with their measurements and styles.
welcome.p3: Create orders: pick the client and garments, take measurements, choose styles, set the price.
welcome.p4: Track fittings, payments and delivery, and share the order as a PDF.
welcome.tip: Swipe or tap Next to continue. You can reopen this tutorial anytime from Profile → App tutorial.

garments.title: What is a garment?
garments.body: A garment is a reusable template for something you sew: a suit jacket, trousers, a dress, a shirt, a coat. You set it up once and use it in every order.
garments.p1: It decides which measurements you take for that piece (e.g. chest, waist, sleeve length).
garments.p2: It holds the styles & materials the client can choose from: fabrics, buttons, lapels, pockets, linings…
garments.p3: An order can contain several garments, e.g. a jacket and trousers for one suit.
garments.p4: Each order keeps a copy of the garment as it was, so changing a garment later never alters old orders.
garments.tip: Start with the 2–3 pieces you make most often. You can add more anytime.

addGarment.title: How to add a garment
addGarment.body: Garments live under Profile → Garments / Templates. When you have none yet, the Home screen also shows an Add Garment button.
addGarment.p1: Open Profile → Garments / Templates and tap New garment.
addGarment.p2: Type a name (e.g. Jacket) and, if you like, a short description. Save.
addGarment.p3: Tap the garment in the list to open it and set up its measurements and styles (next steps).
addGarment.p4: Use the Enabled switch to hide a garment from new orders without deleting it. Duplicate a garment to quickly make a variation.

measurements.title: Choose what to measure
measurements.body: Inside a garment, the Measurements section is the list of points you take from the client for that piece.
measurements.p1: Tap Add measurement and enter its name, e.g. Shoulder width.
measurements.p2: Pick a type: Number (most measurements), Text (a free note), Select (choose from options like Slim, Regular, Loose) or Calculated (worked out from other measurements with a formula).
measurements.p3: Mark the essential ones as Required so they can't be skipped in an order.
measurements.p4: Put them in the order you measure; that's the order you'll fill them in with the client.
measurements.p5: A measurement already used in orders can't be deleted, which protects your history.
measurements.tip: The unit (cm or inches) comes from your general settings and applies to all measurements.

styles.title: Add styles and materials
styles.body: Each garment also has a Styles & Materials section: the options your client chooses from. They're organised into categories, and each category holds items.
styles.p1: Categories group options, e.g. Fabrics, Buttons, Lapels, Pockets, Linings. Tap Add Category, give it a name and pick an icon.
styles.p2: Tap a category, then Add Item. Give it a name (e.g. Italian Wool Super 120s), an optional code and description, and a photo or a colour.
styles.p3: Drag categories and items to put the ones you use most at the top.
styles.p4: Items marked System default can't be deleted, but you can disable the ones you don't offer.
styles.p5: When you create an order, the client's choices are picked in the Summary step and printed on the order PDF.
styles.tip: A photo of each fabric or button makes choosing much easier when you're with the client.

clients.title: Add your clients
clients.body: Every order belongs to a client. Their details, orders and latest measurements are kept together on the client's page.
clients.p1: On Home, tap the + button and choose Add Client. You can also add a new client while creating an order.
clients.p2: Only first name, last name and phone are required. Email, address, notes and a reference photo are optional.
clients.p3: Set a measurement appointment and TailorCraft reminds you 2 hours before.
clients.p4: Open a client from Orders or Home to see all their orders and measurements in one place.

orders.title: Create an order
orders.body: Tap + on Home and choose Create Order. The order is built in a few short steps, and you can go back to any step before saving.
orders.p1: Client: choose an existing client or enter a new one.
orders.p2: Garments: select one or more garments for this order. Disabled garments can't be picked.
orders.p3: Measurements: fill in each garment's measurements. They're prefilled from the client's last order, so you only update what changed. You can also add a sketch: draw it, import a photo, or reuse one.
orders.p4: Summary: pick the styles & materials, enter the total price, the amount paid and the expected delivery date.
orders.p5: Save. The order gets a number and appears under Orders.
orders.tip: Values you type in an order are saved with that order only. They never change the garment's default settings.

tracking.title: Track fittings, payments & delivery
tracking.body: Open any order from the Orders tab to manage it until it's delivered.
tracking.p1: Update the status as you work: Pending → In progress → Completed → Delivered.
tracking.p2: Add fittings with date and time, and mark them Completed, Missed or Cancelled. You get a reminder before each one.
tracking.p3: Update the amount paid as the client pays; the order shows how much is still due on pickup.
tracking.p4: Generate the order PDF with measurements, styles and sketch, and share it with the client or your workshop.
tracking.p5: Orders past their delivery date are flagged as overdue, and the filters on Orders help you find unpaid ones.

more.title: Gallery, calendar & finances
more.body: A few more places that help you run the atelier.
more.p1: Gallery: keep photos of your finished work to show clients.
more.p2: Calendar: see fittings and measurement appointments by day.
more.p3: Financial (from Home): money still owed by clients, expenses and profit.
more.p4: Profile: company details for documents, garments, settings (units, language, currency, theme) and your subscription.

done.title: Let's set up your first garment
done.body: The best first step is a garment you make often. Once it has measurements and a few styles, you can take your first order.
done.p1: Create a garment → add its measurements → add styles & materials.
done.p2: Add a client → create an order.
done.p3: You can reopen this tutorial anytime from Profile → App tutorial.
